html:
SMTO-EXE-0187 — This document is too big or busy for SMTO to process

GUID: 8af38c42-1d50-5023-be98-1cb2f8ead9d3
Slug: office-resource-limit-exceeded
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: office

What happened

  • The file, or the amount of content SMTO was asked to return, was more than SMTO's document tool handles in one step, or too many document steps were running at once. Your original file wasn't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If other tasks are working on Word, Excel or PowerPoint files on the same Gateway, wait for them to finish, then ask SMTO again. A Gateway works on at most four documents at the same time and turns away extra ones.
  2. Ask SMTO for a smaller part at a time, such as one sheet, a few slides, or the first 50 paragraphs. Each step has a limit on how much content it can send back, so smaller requests fit.
  3. If the file is larger than about 30 MB, save a smaller copy in Word, Excel or PowerPoint, for example by compressing pictures or splitting it into several files. SMTO won't open files over 32 MB or files whose contents expand to more than 64 MB.
  4. If you are adding a picture to a slide, use a PNG or JPEG under 8 MB and under about 16 megapixels. Larger pictures go over the size limit for inserted images.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finishes the smaller step and returns its result or reports the new file it created.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the file's size and what you asked for, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't remove content from your only copy of the file; make changes in a copy.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Office processing exceeded a size, structure, result, concurrency or worker resource limit, or the isolated parser worker exited unsuccessfully without naming the exact limit.

What this means

  • Office processing exceeded file/package/XML/argument/result limits, active-operation capacity or worker resource bounds; an unsuccessful worker exit can also map to this category without identifying the exact resource. Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.

Why this can happen

  • Office processing exceeded file/package/XML/argument/result limits, active-operation capacity or worker resource bounds; an unsuccessful worker exit can also map to this category without identifying the exact resource.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the applicable byte, part, compression, node/depth, time or concurrency bound; do not assume every worker failure is a large document.

How to fix it

  • Limits per operation: 32 MiB file, 64 MiB uncompressed, 16 MiB per part, 2,048 parts, 200:1 compression ratio, 250,000 XML nodes and depth 128, 2 MiB request/result envelope, 45-second deadline, 1 GiB worker memory, 8 MiB / 16 MP inserted images, and at most 4 concurrent Office operations per Gateway. Wait for active Office work to finish, reduce the file or request a smaller page/range with offset/limit, and treat a non-zero worker exit as possibly memory/CPU exhaustion.
  • Inspect the specific bound or worker failure. Reduce document/projection size when appropriate, or let active work settle; keep required output complete.

Retry and execution caution

  • Reduce document size or request a smaller range/projection. Limits: 32 MiB file, 64 MiB inflated, 16 MiB part, 2048 parts, 200:1 compression, 250000 XML nodes and 45 seconds.

How to verify the fix

  • A valid smaller operation or supported resource prerequisite completes within the existing bounds.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
